pride_data.title: Identification of host targets of Vpu based on APEX2 proximity labeling
pride_data.projectDescription: The HIV-1 accessory proteins Vpu antagonize a variety of host restriction factors, thus leading to the escape of host immune surveillance and the promotion of virus release. However, the interaction between Vpu and the host proteins has not been fully clarified. Here, we utilized APEX2-based proximity labeling and transmission electron microscope, as well as Immunoprecipitation-Mass spectrometry to characterize the interaction between HIV-1 Vpu and host proteins. We identified 21 cellular targets of Vpu and found the targets were enriched in RNA transport and spliceosome pathway.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: HeLa cells were transfected with pcDNA3.1-Vpu-APEX2 or pcDNA3.1-NES-APEX2 plasmid. Twenty-four hours after transfection, cells were incubated with 500 mM biotin tyramide (Sigma), followed by the addition of H2O2 at a final concentration of 1 mM at room temperature to initiate biotinylation. The reaction was then quenched in quencher solution (5 mM Trolox, 10 mM ascorbic acid, and 10 mM Sodium azide in PBS). After the final quenching, cells were collected and lysed in RIPA buffer (Solarbio) containing protease inhibitor cocktail (Promega) on ice. Lysates were centrifuged at 12,000 g at 4℃ and supernatant was collected. After the determination of protein concentration using Pierce 660-nm protein assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific), the supernatant was incubated with streptavidin magnetic beads overnight at 4°C. The beads were washed twice with RIPA lysis buffer, once with 1 M KCl, once with 0.1 M Sodium Carbonate, once with 2 M urea (in 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0), and twice with RIPA lysis buffer. AlexaFluor 568 conjugated Streptavidin (Thermo Fisher Scientific) was used then to monitor the biotinylation of proteins. For the on-bead digestion, beads were washed twice with 50 mM Tris-HCl buffer (pH=7.5) and twice with 2 M urea/50 mM Tris buffer (pH=7.5). After washing, beads were incubated for 1 hour at room temperature with trypsin in 2 M urea/50mM Tris buffer containing 1 mM DTT. After pre-digestion, beads were washed two times with 2 M urea/50mM Tris buffer. The eluted supernatant was reduced with 4 mM DTT at room temperature. Following reduction, the sample was alkylated with 10 mM iodoacetamide for 45 min and digested overnight at room temperature in trypsin solution.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The data was collected by the Xcalibur3.0 software, and proteomics data were analyzed using the Proteome Discovery searching algorithm (Version 1.4).Mass spectrometry data were analyzed using Microsoft excel 2016 and R Studio (R v.4.0.3). Significance for proteomics data were assessed by Student’s t-test and variance was assessed by an F-test to ensure the correct statistical assumptions were used.
